name: Lechaschau
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy residential community near Reutte, with direct access to the Lech-Radweg and stunning Alpenpanorama.
beschreibung:
Overview

Lechaschau is a lively municipality in the Tyrolean Außerfern within the Reutte district, situated at an altitude of 846 metres directly along the western bank of the wild Lech River. Home to approximately 2,100 residents, the village lies immediately opposite the district capital Reutte, nestling against the wooded flanks of Mount Hahnenkamm and the imposing Gehrenspitze in the Tannheim Mountains. As an integral component of the Nature Park Tyrolean Lech and a key staging post on the long-distance Lechweg trail, Lechaschau unites untouched alpine river wilderness with superb local infrastructure. Extensive riverside meadows, warm Tyrolean hospitality, and direct access to mountain networks make it a preferred hub for active holidays.

History

Permanent settlement in the fertile river pastures west of the Lech began during the High Middle Ages, with the village first documented around 1430 under the name Lech Aschaw, meaning "ash tree meadow on the Lech". For generations, local livelihoods depended upon forestry, timber rafting, and subsistence agriculture, constantly contending with the unpredictable floodwaters of the untamed alpine river. During the 19th century, Lechaschau flourished as an artisanal and farming community. An architectural milestone was achieved in 1963–1964 with the construction of the Holy Spirit parish church, notable for its striking modernist expressionist architecture and contemporary stained-glass windows. Today, Lechaschau thrives as a welcoming community with rich cultural traditions.

Getting There

Lechaschau enjoys prime accessibility from both Austria and neighbouring Germany. Motorists arriving from Germany follow the toll-free A7 motorway through Füssen and the border tunnel straight into the Reutte basin, crossing the Lech bridge into Lechaschau. From Innsbruck, drivers travel via the A12 Inntal Autobahn across the scenic Fern Pass on the B179 highway to the Reutte exit. Rail travelers take the historic Außerfern Railway to Reutte in Tirol station, from where Lechaschau is accessible within a brief walk across the pedestrian bridge or via frequent regional transit buses.

Tips

Walking a section of the Lechweg trail through the protected Lechaschauer Lechauen reveals one of Central Europe's last genuine wild river habitats, featuring unique gravel banks and diverse bird species. In summer, the scenic open-air river bathing area provides refreshing cooling off. Mountain hikers can ascend Mount Hahnenkamm via the Cillyhütte or Schneetalalm refuges, rewarded by grand panoramic views overlooking the entire Reutte valley basin. Just across the river, the record-breaking highline179 suspension footbridge and the medieval Ehrenberg Castle ruins offer an extraordinary historical adventure.
